items.title: 67259_Big Chief Moore oral history interview
items.q: I got a lot of respect for my aunt Mary because she taught me as much piano as she could

ctx.x: Before breakfast, we used to play long tones. He'd be off to work, and I'd be off to school. That's how I, I learned. And then, my aunt would set me on the piano: set next, she sat next to me, and I'd be looking out, out the, out the window, and the kids would be play- ing baseball; I want to get out there, and my mind is ten miles away. And a, in fact, in fact my goodness, in fact where - when my aunt would know that I wasn't paying attention, she would kind of slap me, behind me, behind the ear. She practically…
too. And I got a lot of respect for my aunt Mary because she taught me as much piano as she could, and then I had to go to get another teacher.
I see. After school did you, after classes were over at school, did you play in a school orchestra, or did you come home and practice more?
